Published online:

Geographic focus:

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical observation [YES] — Q2 2026 earnings results reported
T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES] — M&A pipeline, dealmaking momentum, private credit outlook
T3. Long-term development [YES] — AI infrastructure investment cycle, asset/wealth management build-out

Synopsis:
Goldman Sachs delivered a blowout Q2 2026, with EPS of $20.98 vs. $14.48 consensus — a massive beat. Equities revenue hit a record $7.42B (+72% YoY), driven by volatility from the U.S.-Iran war and inflation/rate uncertainty. Investment banking fees surged 55% to $3.4B, fueled by a record M&A wave — Goldman advised on $1.2T in deals H1 2026, $425B ahead of its nearest rival. Fixed income jumped 32%. Asset & wealth management rose 20%. GS shares hit an all-time high, up 7.2%. CEO Solomon highlighted the AI infrastructure investment cycle as a sustained multi-year tailwind for strategic activity and capital markets.
